item.title: Statement by Members of the High-Level Mission of OAS Member States to Bolivia
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesperson
item.description:
Office of the Spokesperson

Statement by Members of the High-Level Mission of OAS Member States to Bolivia

Media Note

July 30, 2026

The text of the following statement will be released by the Governments of the United States of America, Argentina, Canada, Chile, Panama, Peru, and Uruguay.

At the invitation of the Government of the Plurinational State of Bolivia and pursuant to the resolution adopted by the General Assembly of the Organization of American States, members of the High-Level Mission traveled to La Paz and Santa Cruz de la Sierra on July 29-30.  We thank the Government of Bolivia, Foreign Minister Fernando Aramayo, members of Bolivia’s civil society, and all participants for their hospitality and engagement. 

While we respect the right to peaceful protest, we are deeply concerned by the impact of violent blockades on the lives of Bolivian citizens, democracy, and the rule of law in Bolivia. The continued efforts to undermine and overthrow the legitimate and democratically elected government of President Rodrigo Paz represent a serious threat to constitutional order and democratic stability in the country and our hemisphere. 

A minority acting outside the law attempted to disregard the will expressed by the majority of Bolivians at the polls less than one year ago, rejected the government’s willingness to engage in dialogue, and maintained road blockades for more than seven weeks, depriving the Bolivian people of access to food, health care, and other necessities such as fuel.  These actions severely affected the daily lives of millions of citizens and put fundamental rights at risk.  Deaths of Bolivian civilians occurred due to restrictions on free transit, which prevented them from accessing medicines, hospitals, or health centers in a timely manner.  Protesters injured police officers in the line of duty.  For any democracy to function, violence cannot subvert the constitutional order. 

We value the government’s willingness to engage in dialogue and in finding agreements. We express solidarity and support the constitutionally elected Bolivian government and urge the prioritization of dialogue and negotiations within the established constitutional framework as a fundamental tool of democracy. We urge peaceful resolution of conflicts without violence.

Defending freedom, democracy, and hemispheric security requires commitment and cooperation.  During this Mission, we reaffirm our commitment to continue working to strengthen stability and preserve the democratic order in our region and stand in solidarity with Bolivia’s democratic government and the people of Bolivia. We call for peaceful coexistence through consensus-building and dialogue.

This statement reflects the experiences of the members of the Mission, who will report their findings to their respective governments, consult with other OAS member states on actionable items to support the democratically elected government of Bolivia, including a report-back to the OAS Permanent Council, and collaborate through the OAS in close regional coordination on next steps.

item.title: United States Sanctioning Iran’s Mahan Air Network and IRGC-Linked Front Company
item.dc:creator: Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, Spokesperson
item.description:
Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, Spokesperson

United States Sanctioning Iran’s Mahan Air Network and IRGC-Linked Front Company

Press Statement

July 30, 2026

The United States today sanctioned six entities and individuals in China, India, Russia, and Iran that enable the Iranian regime’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). These include entities that support Mahan Air, the IRGC’s airline of choice for moving weapons, military personnel, and equipment. Today’s action also targets DadeNegar Startup Studio, an IRGC-affiliated front company supporting Iranian military targeting by soliciting locations of American and Israeli equipment in the Middle East.

The United States calls on the international community, particularly companies and individuals doing business with Mahan Air or any other sanctioned Iranian carrier, to recognize the serious risks raised by continuing such engagement.

The United States will continue to expose and disrupt entities providing the IRGC with the tools and information it uses to threaten American personnel, our partners, and regional stability.

 OFAC is taking this action pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13224, as amended, which targets terrorist groups, their supporters, and those who aid acts of terrorism, and in furtherance of the President’s National Security Presidential Memorandum 2 (NSPM-2), which directs the U.S. government to deny the IRGC access to assets and resources that sustain its destabilizing activities. On October 12, 2011, OFAC designated Mahan Air pursuant to E.O. 13224 for providing financial, material, and technological support to Iran’s IRGC-Qods Force (IRGC-QF), which OFAC designated pursuant to E.O. 13224 in October 2007 for providing material support to multiple terrorist organizations. The U.S. Department of State designated the IRGC itself pursuant to the counterproliferation authority E.O. 13382 in 2007, and OFAC designated the IRGC pursuant to E.O. 13224 in October 2017 for providing support to the IRGC-QF. For more information on today’s action, please see Treasury’s press releases.

item.title: Celebrating America’s 250th: State Department Launches Commemorative Passports Nationwide
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesperson
item.description:
Office of the Spokesperson

Celebrating America’s 250th: State Department Launches Commemorative Passports Nationwide

Media Note

July 30, 2026

In response to overwhelming demand, the Department of State is making an additional 250,000 of the special commemorative passports available to the public.  Americans all across the country will now have the opportunity to apply for one of these additional special passports, known as the “Patriot Passport.”  

Since its release in celebration of 250 years of American independence, the commemorative passport has generated extraordinary public interest.  The Department of State is responding by expanding access so Americans across the country can obtain this unique and special document.  The Department is hosting application events at passport agencies and centers for patriots all across our nation.   

The commemorative passport features custom artwork connecting America’s past to the present, including a portrait of President Donald J. Trump alongside the text of the Declaration of Independence, a Freedom 250 gold flag, and an image of the Founding Fathers signing the Declaration of Independence. 

Appointments are required to apply for the “Patriot Passport.”  To learn about application events near you and how to schedule an appointment, visit travel.state.gov/passport250.

item.title: Morocco Throne Day
item.dc:creator: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
item.description:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Morocco Throne Day

Press Statement

July 30, 2026

On behalf of the United States of America, I extend my warmest greetings to His Majesty King Mohammed VI and to the people of Morocco on the anniversary of His Majesty’s ascension to the throne.

For nearly 250 years, the United States and Morocco have shared the longest friendship in American history. This is a strong and enduring partnership built on shared values and a common commitment to peace, security, and prosperity.

Under President Trump’s leadership, the United States has been unequivocal: we recognize Moroccan sovereignty over Western Sahara and support Morocco’s serious, credible, and realistic Autonomy Proposal as the only basis for a just, lasting, and mutually acceptable solution. Any other path prolongs the status quo and is unacceptable. Genuine autonomy under Moroccan sovereignty provides this region and the continent with the chance to finally move forward after 50 years. This dispute must end now, and the United States will continue to push toward that goal. American diplomacy remains focused on a mutually beneficial solution for all who call this region home.

Under His Majesty’s leadership, Morocco has been an anchor of regional stability and security, including through its vital role in the Abraham Accords. The United States deeply values this partnership and looks forward to strengthening our work together to secure the Sahel. Your vision for economic growth will create new prosperity for both our peoples, and President Trump has directed his administration to encourage economic and social development with Morocco, including in the Western Sahara territory. As we look toward the next 250 years of friendship, the United States will remain your trusted partner in energy, artificial intelligence, critical minerals, and defense.

Together, we will continue to advance peace, regional stability, and economic growth that benefits both our peoples.

item.title: U.S. Department of State and U.S. Department of Health and Human Services on Strengthening Vaccine Safety, Accountability, and American Leadership in Global Health
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesperson
item.description:
Office of the Spokesperson

U.S. Department of State and U.S. Department of Health and Human Services on Strengthening Vaccine Safety, Accountability, and American Leadership in Global Health

Media Note

July 29, 2026

The United States is committed to advancing global health in a manner that reflects American interests, scientific integrity, and accountability to the American people.  Under President Trump’s leadership, the United States has made clear that American taxpayer dollars must support transparent, evidence-based programs that deliver measurable health outcomes.

Last year, President Trump directed Secretary of Health and Human Services Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. and Secretary of State Marco Rubio to engage directly with Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance (Gavi), and secure meaningful reforms before the United States would consider future support.  Those discussions resulted in significant commitments that strengthen vaccine safety, improve public health, and better align Gavi’s work with the principles of Gold Standard Science and transparency.  Based on those commitments, the United States will immediately release all $600 million in Congressionally appropriated funds to Gavi for both FY25 and FY26. 

Gavi has committed to work towards transitioning mercury-containing vaccines and expanding access to newer, mercury-free alternatives.  Specifically, in partnership with Gavi’s Board and countries, Gavi will make every effort to:

  • transition mercury-containing meningococcal A vaccines with mercury-free vaccines that protect against additional meningococcal strains;
  • transition mercury-containing pentavalent DTP-Hib-HepB vaccines to mercury-free hexavalent vaccines that also protect against polio;
  • transition mercury-containing pneumococcal vaccines to mercury-free vaccines that protect against additional pneumococcal strains; and
  • transition mercury-containing hepatitis B vaccines to mercury-free alternatives.

The Administration believes reducing reliance on mercury-containing vaccines, where suitable alternatives are available, is a pro-vaccine, pro-innovation policy.  The United States and the European Union removed mercury from most childhood vaccines 25 years ago.  As of June 2025, CDC’s Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices no longer recommends any mercury-containing vaccines.  Children in Africa, Asia, and Latin America deserve access to the same higher-quality, mercury-free vaccines, and these changes will also expand protection against additional disease strains.

Achieving these transitions will require manufacturers to expand production capacity, countries to adopt newer vaccine formulations, and Gavi’s governing Board to complete the necessary approvals.  The United States recognizes these implementation challenges but welcomes Gavi’s commitment to work toward these goals through transparent governance and responsible stewardship.

Gavi has already implemented additional reforms requested by the United States including:

  • Ending the promotion and procurement of COVID-19 vaccines for routine immunization programs; and
  • Finalizing extensive operational reforms including the reorganization and downsizing of staff in Geneva and instituting a partnership accountability framework that decreases funding for and reforms Gavi’s engagement with other partners, including the World Health Organization (WHO).

Gavi has further committed to establishing an integrated and dedicated Secretariat function to monitor and review developments in vaccine science, including vaccine safety.  In addition, given the sizeable contribution the United States is making to improve access to vaccines, the United States expects to resume its place on the Gavi Board.  In this role, the United States will continue to hold Gavi accountable for measurable progress toward these commitments.  It will evaluate any future U.S. support based on demonstrated performance, accountability, and implementation of these reforms.

The United States also reaffirms that it will not provide U.S. Government funding to the World Health Organization through Gavi.

President Trump has made clear that American leadership in global health must be rooted in accountability, scientific excellence, and measurable results.  The Department of Health and Human Services and the Department of State will continue to ensure that U.S. global health programs and partnerships uphold Gold Standard Science, rigorous independent review, transparency, responsible stewardship of taxpayer resources, and better health outcomes around the world.

item.title: Opportunities for Growth in U.S.-Peru Relations
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesperson
item.description:
Office of the Spokesperson

Opportunities for Growth in U.S.-Peru Relations

Fact Sheet

July 29, 2026

The Presidential Delegation to the July 28 inauguration of President Fujimori, led by Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau, signals U.S. commitment to Peru and highlights the strength of our partnership. The strong ties between the United States and Peru are underpinned by an enduring friendship spanning 200 years of diplomatic relations. The Trump Administration looks forward to working with President Fujimori to bring security and prosperity to the United States, Peru, and to our hemisphere.  

Enhancing Security

The United States applauds President Fujimori’s focus on fighting transnational criminal organizations that threaten American and Peruvian security and prosperity and to improve citizen security across Peru.   

  • Peru is a valuable member of the Americans Counter-Cartel Coalition (A3C), and the Department of War intends to scale up counter-narcotics cooperation with Peru, particularly in the northern tri-border region.  
  • The Department of State’s Bureau of Counterterrorism will send a Department of Justice team to Peru to improve bilateral coordination and information sharing on efforts to combat the Tren de Aragua, which President Trump designated as a Foreign Terrorist Organization (FTO). 
  • The Bureau of Counterterrorism will also help disrupt FTO operations by supporting President Fujimori’s border security efforts through the expansion of biometrics collection in prisons and border regions and the donation of two Explosive Trace Detection machines to Jorge Chavez International Airport.  
  • The Department of Commerce will convene U.S. industry partners in Lima in September to discuss opportunities for U.S. technology providers under President Fujimori’s plans to construct nine new prisons.   
  • The Department of State’s Bureau of International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Affairs (INL) has a long and successful history of working with Peru tocombat narco-trafficking, illegal mining, and other illicit activities. With newly created and expanded vetted units, we can effectively support President Fujimori’s efforts to dismantle organized crime groups.     
  • The newly created, INL-funded Peruvian National Police (PNP) Complex Crime Investigative Unit vetted unit, managed by FBI, will carry out complex organized crime investigations.  
  • Following two years of successful operations against transnational criminal organizations, we expanded the PNP Transnational Criminal Investigative Unit, run by DHS and supported by State. 
  • INL will provide additional specialized training and equipment to help Peru combat illegal mining and associated criminal activities. 

Increasing Trade and Investment

Peru’s stable economy has attracted U.S. investment across multiple sectors, and President Fujimori’s pro-business plans will create opportunities for the U.S. private sector and strengthen Peru’s economic growth.   

  • Ambassador Navarro will lead a “Peru is Open for Business” trade mission to the United States this year.  In addition, the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) is actively seeking investment opportunities in energy, infrastructure, critical minerals, and other priority sectors and will send a business development mission to Peru this year.
  • To increase our collaboration in emerging technology, the United States will host an AI Summit on September 8 in Lima.  The Department of War will provide a cyber-advisor to work side by side with the Fujimori government on cyber security issues.   
  • To identify new areas for cooperation in mining, the United States and Peru will establish a critical minerals working group to implement the Critical Minerals MOU signed in February.  An up to $5 million DFC investment in Peru’s mining sector will support the establishment of the reprocessing plant, which will enhance processing technologies and refining capacity in Peru, strengthening the supply chain for critical minerals.
  • To improve Peru’s port infrastructure, the United States will continue to support the expansion of the Port of Callao – Peru’s most consequential port – through the work of the Army Corps of Engineers. We will also work with the Fujimori administration to identify opportunities for U.S. industry to invest in the port’s growth and future success.    

Space Cooperation

The United States will expand on decades of successful cooperation to advance science, education, and development of the global space industry.  Peru has taken a leadership role in the Artemis Accords.  We look forward to expanding civil, commercial, and defense related space cooperation that enhance American and Peruvian prosperity and security, including:  

  • Developing, together with Peru, a space consortium – a public-private effort focused on education, military, civilian, and commercial opportunities – to grow Peru’s space economy. 
  • Sending a Peruvian liaison officer to work directly with U.S. Space Command.   
  • Assisting Peru in finalizing their 10-year space strategy.   
  • Donating a high-powered telescope by the end of 2026.   
  • Providing additional scholarships for education in space-related disciplines such as engineering, aerospace, astrophysics, cyber-security, and related fields.  

Disaster Preparedness and Relief

The United States stands ready to help Peru strengthen its preparedness to respond to El Niño weather events.  We applaud President Fujimori for developing a comprehensive response plan.   

  • The United States has pre-positioned emergency blankets and hygiene kits for emergency assistance for quick response.  
  • The Department of War will donate mobile bridges to assist with potential floods and continue to upgrade several of the 18 regional emergency communication centers originally built under the Humanitarian Assistance Program.
  • FEMA will lead a series of virtual workshops for Peru on disaster risk management. The USNS Comfort Hospital Ship will visit Peru in early 2027, augmenting Peru’s capacity to provide medical support.

We will also work with the Fujimori administration to identify opportunities for U.S. industry to invest in the port’s growth and future success.    

Space Cooperation

The United States will expand on decades of successful cooperation to advance science, education, and development of the global space industry.  Peru has taken a leadership role in the Artemis Accords.  We look forward to expanding civil, commercial, and defense related space cooperation that enhance American and Peruvian prosperity and security, including:  

  • Developing, together with Peru, a space consortium – a public-private effort focused on education, military, civilian, and commercial opportunities – to grow Peru’s space economy. 
  • Sending a Peruvian liaison officer to work directly with U.S. Space Command.   
  • Assisting Peru in finalizing their 10-year space strategy.   
  • Donating a high-powered telescope by the end of 2026.   
  • Providing additional scholarships for education in space-related disciplines such as engineering, aerospace, astrophysics, cyber-security, and related fields.  

Disaster Preparedness and Relief

The United States stands ready to help Peru strengthen its preparedness to respond to El Niño weather events.  We applaud President Fujimori for developing a comprehensive response plan.   

  • The United States has pre-positioned emergency blankets and hygiene kits for emergency assistance for quick response.  
  • The Department of War will donate mobile bridges to assist with potential floods and continue to upgrade several of the 18 regional emergency communication centers originally built under the Humanitarian Assistance Program.
  • FEMA will lead a series of virtual workshops for Peru on disaster risk management. The USNS Comfort Hospital Ship will visit Peru in early 2027, augmenting Peru’s capacity to provide medical support.

item.dc:creator: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
item.description:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Republic of Vanuatu National Day

Press Statement

July 29, 2026

On behalf of the United States, I offer a heartfelt congratulations to the ni-Vanuatu people on their 46th National Day.

The United States and Vanuatu have made significant strides in our bilateral relationship over the past year. We have deepened our commercial ties, encouraging economic development and ensuring mutual prosperity. The United States is committed to building on our successful law enforcement collaboration and addressing our shared security challenges.

I look forward to further strengthening our relationship and wish you and all ni-Vanuatu the best on your joyous day.

Secretary Rubio’s Meeting with Kazakh Minister of Foreign Affairs Kosherbayev

Readout

July 29, 2026

The below is attributable to Spokesperson Tommy Pigott:

Secretary Rubio spoke today with Kazakh Minister of Foreign Affairs Yermek Kosherbayev. The two officials discussed the importance of energy security, including the reliable and uninterrupted export of Kazakhstan-origin oil via the Caspian Pipeline Consortium, for regional stability and prosperity.  The Secretary expressed his appreciation for Kazakhstan’s strong support for President Trump’s peace initiatives, and his interest in deepening bilateral economic cooperation.

item.title: Countering Iran’s Exploitation of the Strait of Hormuz
item.dc:creator: Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, Spokesperson
item.description:
Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, Spokesperson

Countering Iran’s Exploitation of the Strait of Hormuz

Press Statement

July 29, 2026

Today, the United States designated the Persian Gulf Marine Insurance Company and Hormuz Safe Marine Services Authority, two Iranian entities backed by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), for running coercive “insurance” schemes that extort international shipping transiting the Strait of Hormuz.  These entities manufacture risk—including the threat of vessel seizures—and then charge commercial vessels for coverage against dangers created by the regime itself, generating revenue that sustains IRGC operations and Iran’s broader campaign of regional destabilization.

The United States also designated eight companies operating vessels that have transported illicit Iranian crude oil and petrochemical products to China and the United Arab Emirates.  These vessels form part of Iran’s “shadow fleet,” which the regime relies on to evade sanctions.

Today’s designations support the U.S. Navy’s enforcement of a blockade on Iranian ports and coastline and add to a sustained campaign that has now sanctioned more than 100 vessels this year.

The United States will continue to hold Iran accountable for weaponizing vital international waterways and evading sanctions through shadow fleet operations and deceptive financial schemes.  Protecting navigational rights and freedoms in the Strait of Hormuz is a global interest, and the United States will act, alongside partners, to ensure Iran cannot hold international commerce hostage to finance its malign activities.  We will continue working with allies to isolate the regime diplomatically and economically until it ceases its destabilizing behavior.

Today’s action was taken pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13902, which targets Iran’s financial, petroleum, and petrochemical sectors.  It continues the robust sanctions campaign targeting Iranian oil sales in support of the President’s National Security Presidential Memorandum 2 (NSPM-2).  For more information on today’s action, please see the Department of the Treasury’s press release.

item.title: Deputy Secretary Landau’s Travel to Peru
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesperson
item.description:
Office of the Spokesperson

Deputy Secretary Landau’s Travel to Peru

Media Note

July 26, 2026

Deputy Secretary Christopher Landau will lead the U.S. delegation to the July 28 inauguration of President-elect Keiko Fujimori in Lima, Peru.  During the visit, Deputy Secretary Landau will meet with President-elect Fujimori and other senior Peruvian officials to reaffirm our 200-year diplomatic partnership with Peru.  The meetings will focus on expanding cooperation on security, investment, and disaster preparedness – advancing shared prosperity and strengthening regional stability.

Members of the Presidential Delegation include:

  • H. Christopher Landau, Deputy Secretary of State, U.S. Department of State
  • H. Bernie Navarro, Ambassador of the United States to the Republic of Peru
  • H. William Kimmitt, Under Secretary for International Trade, U.S. Department of Commerce
  • Erin Browne, Counselor to the Secretary of the Treasury
  • Viviana Bovo, Senior Advisor for Western Hemisphere Affairs, U.S. Department of State
